text: So let us fear that, while the promise of entering his rest still stands, any of you should be found to have fallen short of it.

versions.text: So let us be on our guard: since the promise of entering his rest still stands, none of you should be found to have fallen short of it.
versions.explanation: Φοβηθῶμεν is a hortatory subjunctive of fear ("let us fear"); "be on our guard" weakens the emotional force of the warning. Also, the Greek construction with μήποτε makes the falling short the object of fear rather than a separate command, which the revision preserves.

text: For we have had the good news preached to us just as they did; but the word they heard did them no good, because they were not united by faith with those who listened.

versions.text: For we have had the good news preached to us just as they did; but the word they heard did them no good, because it was not joined with faith in those who heard it.
versions.explanation: The accusative plural participle συγκεκερασμένους agrees with ἐκείνους ("those people"), not with ὁ λόγος, so the sense is that the hearers were not joined by faith to those who truly listened. If the current rendering is retained, a footnote noting the alternative reading and translation would help the reader.

text: We who have believed do enter that rest, just as he has said: "As I swore in my anger, they shall never enter my rest" — and yet his works were finished from the foundation of the world.
For somewhere he says this about the seventh day: "And on the seventh day God rested from all his works."
And again in this same passage he says, "They shall never enter my rest."

versions.text: And in the other passage he says, "They shall never enter my rest."
versions.explanation: ἐν τούτῳ means "in this [passage]" — the writer is quoting the same psalm again, not a different passage. "The other passage" could mislead the hearer into thinking a second text is cited.

text: Since, then, it remains for some to enter it, and since those who first heard the good news did not enter because of their disobedience,
God again appoints a day — "Today" — speaking through David so long afterward, in the words already quoted: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
For if Joshua had given them rest, God would not have spoken later of another day.
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God.
For whoever enters God's rest also rests from his own works, just as God rested from his.
Let us then make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one falls by following the same example of disobedience.

For the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword. It pierces to the point where soul and spirit divide, joints and marrow as well, and it judges the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
No creature is hidden from him; everything lies naked and exposed before the eyes of the one to whom we must give account.
Since, then, we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus the Son of God, let us hold fast to our confession.
For we do not have a high priest unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who was tempted in every way as we are, yet without sin.
So let us approach the throne of grace with confidence, to receive mercy and find grace to help us in our time of need.
